evidence_quotes.quote: the Phiri community in Soweto have approached the court to enforce their rights of access to adequate clean water.
judges with regard to the right to access clean water, the issue of pre-paid water meters, the free basic water policy

rationale: Doctrinal legal commentary analyzing South Africa's constitutional right to water (Section 27), the National Water Act, the Water Services Act, and the Mazibuko v City of Johannesburg litigation across the High Court, Supreme Court of Appeal, and Constitutional Court. Multiple legal/regulatory mechanisms are co-equally central: (1) fees_tariffs_subsidies (the Free Basic Water Policy's 6 kilolitre/month free household allowance, payment requirements for excess consumption, cross-subsidization, and Indigent Registration Policy arrears write-offs and extra 4 kL allowance), (2) enforcement_sanctions (automatic halting/suspension of water supply via pre-paid water meters upon exhaustion of free basic credit without procedural protections), and (3) review_redress (constitutional right-to-water litigation and loss of administrative hearing/complaint avenues under prepaid metering), with secondary discussion of procedural_burden and participation_assistance in indigent registration. Outcomes centrally span effective_access (sufficiency of daily household water quantity, supply interruptions, fetching burdens, and reliance on contaminated streams) alongside economic_access (household inability to afford prepaid water units) and administrative_outcome (service suspension/disconnection classification and judicial review outcomes).
